figures.caption: The final main pipeline. Count proposals are derived from detection speed; displacement and timing are fitted. Evaluation and sensitivity do not replace the nominal proposal by the lowest-error setting.
The inner fitting procedure. TRF updates only timing; every residual evaluation recomputes the best endpoint-constrained linear displacement fit. The side arrow denotes repeated timing evaluations.
Nominal detection speed, retained peaks and candidate speed-minimum boundaries. The first window proposes K=4 and the second K=3. These are heuristic proposals, not known labels.
First window at K=4. Original and reconstructed XYZ position are shown on the left; numerical XYZ velocity is shown on the right. All methods share the raw target and positional endpoints.

Second window at K=3 using the same evaluation convention. The approximation follows the major Y and Z movement more closely than either same-count uniform control, but misses some X and earlier trajectory details.
First-window detection speed and individual analytical component speed magnitudes. Magnitudes are shown for interpretation; they must not be added as scalars to obtain the total speed.
Second-window detection speed and component speed magnitudes. Overlap is allowed by the fitted onset and completion times; no requirement is imposed that the wrist stop at every proposed boundary.

Errors for every distinct detected partition in the count sweep, with uniform baselines at the same K. Black stars mark the nominal detector setting. The detected partition changes along with K, so the points are not a pure count-only experiment.
Timing-bound sensitivity at fixed nominal counts and boundaries. Narrow, nominal and wide mean (α,β)=(0.30,0.10), (0.45,0.20) and (0.60,0.30). The vertical scales differ between windows.
